newsitem.title: FINLAND: UPM says pulp market still fragile.
newsitem.headline: UPM says pulp market still fragile.

text.p: Uncertainty still reigns on the pulp market and prices will not rise in the near term unless North American market pulp producers reduce their output, forestry group UPM-Kymmene Oy CEO Juha Niemela said on Thursday.

"Demand alone cannot correct the situation in the short term, output stoppages are also needed. It is mainly the North American market pulp producers who should have stoppages," Niemela told a news conference.
"Recent statistics on inventories are promising but insufficient," Niemela said.
UPM is self-sufficient in chemical pulp with an annual capacity of 2.2 million tonnes and it has no significant sales to other paper producers.

Niemela said he did not know whether pulp price hikes announced for October could materialise and he declined to estimate whether softwood pulp prices could reach $600 per tonne from the current unprofitable $560-570 price.
UPM said in September an announced pulp price hike to $620-630 per tonne in October seemed realistic.
